example_prompt: Fetch a Smile Link by its ref_id to check its configuration, expiry and whether it is disabled.

refId.description: The link's id, returned as `ref_id` at creation. Passed as a path parameter.

ref_id.description: The link's id — the reference used on all v3 smile_links routes.

link.description: The URL to hand to the end user.

verification_method.description: The verification product to run for this ID type.

callback_url.description: Where job results for this link are delivered.

disabled_at.description: Set while the link is disabled; null when active.

user_id.description:
The user id a single-use link's job runs under (generated when not
provided). Null on multi-use links — each opener gets its own user
id at link-open.

token_provided_fields.description: Field names bound onto this link from the creating SmileID-Token's payload. Sorted. The hosted flow that opens the link skips collecting these from the end user; empty when the link was created without a bound token payload.

token_provided_values.description: Values for the subset of token_provided_fields held in the clear (country, id_type, consent). PII fields are never returned here — the token holds opaque pii_-prefixed references to them, not the values. Empty object when nothing is bound.

consent.description: The consent record bound from the token. Present only when consent is bound, and complete when present.

gotchas: Two-step auth: first call POST /v3/token with headers SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-API-Key (SMILEID_PARTNER_ID / SMILEID_API_KEY) to get a JWT, then send SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-Token: {token} on this request. The token expires 15 minutes after issuance — Smile ID recommends minting a new one for every verification request rather than reusing it. Never mint tokens in the browser: the API key must stay on your backend.
The Authentication page requires both SmileID-Partner-ID and SmileID-Token on all V3 requests; the endpoint's own OpenAPI only declares SmileID-Token. Send both.
refId is the ref_id (a uuid) returned by create_smile_link; a non-uuid value returns 400, an unknown one 404.
disabled_at is set while the link is disabled and null when active. token_provided_values never contains PII — only country, id_type and consent are returned in the clear.
A product-scoped token is rejected here with 401 ('missing, invalid, or product-scoped token') — mint the token without `product` for this route.

Sandbox base URL is https://testapi.smileidentity.com (this spec uses production, https://api.smileidentity.com). Keys, tokens and callback URLs are environment-specific: a sandbox token returns 401 in production.

spans: Returns the link resource for a link id.
Set while the link is disabled; null when active.
